description: Creamy rice and oat porridge with warm blueberries, cinnamon and walnuts.
method: Put the dry rice, oats, cinnamon and all the measured water in a small covered pan. Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 25–30 minutes, stirring regularly, until the rice and oats are fully tender.
Add all the blueberries and sugar and cook for another 3–4 minutes, crushing some berries into the porridge.
Scatter over all the chopped walnuts and serve the entire bowl. If tracking fluid, measure the finished portion rather than assuming the added water is the fluid allowance.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

description: A savoury rice and potato hash with homemade seitan, peppers and chives.
method: Mix the vital wheat gluten with 35 g of the water into a dough. Knead for 2 minutes, rest for 5 minutes and flatten to about 1 cm thick. Steam over a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes until firm and cooked through, retaining the entire dough.
Cook the rice with the remaining 75 g water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes. Use peeled potato already boiled without salt and drained; weigh 50 g cooked.

Dice the steamed seitan and cooked potato. Finely chop the onion and pepper and cook in all the oil for 6–8 minutes. Add all the seitan, rice and potato and fry for 4–5 minutes until steaming hot. Add the chives and pepper and serve the entire portion.
notes: Pure vital wheat gluten is not ordinary flour. Homemade seitan texture and cooking need a kitchen trial; wheat/gluten allergen applies.

description: A soft tofu scramble with tomatoes, spinach and gentle spices, served with a rice flatbread.
method: Mix the rice flour with 40 g of the water and 5 g of the oil to make a thick batter. Rest for 10 minutes. Spread in a non-stick pan and cook for 3–4 minutes per side until fully cooked as one thin flatbread.

Use regular calcium-sulphate tofu, gently drained without pressing, and crumble the weighed portion. Soften chopped onion in the remaining 10 g oil for 4 minutes, then add cumin and turmeric for 30 seconds.

Add chopped tomato, spinach, tofu and remaining 20 g water. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes until hot and the vegetables are tender. Stir in the parsley and serve all the scramble with the whole flatbread.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

description: A warm homemade wrap filled with seitan, white beans and lemony vegetables.
method: Mix the vital wheat gluten with 35 g water, knead for 2 minutes and rest for 5 minutes. Flatten to 1 cm thick and steam over a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes until firm and cooked throughout. Retain the entire seitan portion.

Mix the plain flour with 20 g water into a dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest for 10 minutes. Roll between non-stick sheets without extra flour and dry-cook for 2–3 minutes per side until fully cooked.
Dice the steamed seitan. Cook shredded cabbage and carrot in all the oil with the cumin and remaining 45 g water for 8–10 minutes. Add the cooked, drained navy beans and seitan and heat through.
Stir in lemon juice, parsley and pepper. Put all the filling and juices in the whole flatbread, fold and serve.
notes: Use pure vital wheat gluten; this is a wheat/gluten-containing recipe.

description: A substantial brunch bowl with homemade seitan, white beans, rice, peppers and walnuts.
method: Mix the vital wheat gluten with 50 g water, knead for 2 minutes and rest for 5 minutes. Flatten to 1 cm thick and steam over a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes until firm and fully cooked.
Simmer the brown rice in 80 g water for 15 minutes. Add the white rice and remaining 45 g water and cook covered for another 12–15 minutes until tender, keeping any liquid.
Dice the seitan. Cook chopped onion and pepper in all the oil for 8 minutes. Add the cooked, drained navy beans and all the seitan and heat through.
Fold in all the rice, chopped walnuts, parsley, lemon juice and pepper. Serve the entire bowl and edible juices.

description: A warm chickpea and carrot flatbread with crunchy cabbage and lemony walnut dressing.
method: Mix the flour with the measured water to make a dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest for 10 minutes. Roll between non-stick sheets without extra flour.
Finely dice the carrot. Cook it in one third of the oil in a covered non-stick pan for 8–10 minutes over low heat. Stir in the cumin and cooked, drained chickpeas, cover and heat through.
Dry-cook the flatbread in a separate hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side until cooked throughout. Finely shred the cabbage and chop the walnuts and parsley.
Mix the remaining oil and lemon juice with the walnuts, parsley and pepper. Serve all the chickpeas, carrot and cabbage on the whole flatbread with all the dressing.

description: Crisp black-bean and corn cakes with a fresh cabbage and lime salad.
method: Use black beans previously boiled without salt and drained. Mash them and mix with the masa harina, sweetcorn, finely chopped onion, cumin and 20 g of the measured water. Form three thin cakes.
Heat three quarters of the oil in a non-stick pan. Cook the cakes over medium-low heat for 5–6 minutes per side until firm, fully cooked and steaming hot.
Shred the cabbage and dice the tomato. Mix the lime juice, remaining oil, remaining 15 g water and chopped coriander into a dressing. Serve all the cakes with all the slaw and dressing.
notes: Brazilian-inspired bean and corn cakes; masa harina is a declared adaptation.

Cook the vegetables in two thirds of the oil with the thyme and pepper for 8–10 minutes, retaining their juices. Stir in the ricotta and lemon juice off the heat.

Spoon over all the filling and chopped walnuts, fold in the sides and warm for 1–2 minutes. Serve the whole galette.

description: Hand-folded dumplings with cabbage, mushrooms, white beans and ricotta.
method: Mix 50 g of the flour with 30 g of the water and one third of the oil. Knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 15 minutes.

Finely chop the cabbage, mushrooms and onion. Cook in the remaining oil and remaining 15 g water for 10–12 minutes until tender. Mash in the cooked, drained navy beans and ricotta. Mix the remaining 5 g flour with the filling and cook for 2 minutes to thicken; season with pepper and cool.
Roll the dough between non-stick sheets without extra flour. Cut six circles. Divide all the filling among them, fold and pinch the edges firmly.
Poach in a separate pan of unsalted water for 3–4 minutes after the dumplings float, checking the dough is fully cooked. Lift out, turn in the melted butter and serve all six with any loose filling.
Use vegetarian-rennet cheese for the vegetarian version specified here.
notes: Boiling water is a discarded process aid. No nutrient reduction is credited for poaching.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.
allergenNote: Recipe-ingredient flags only. Check actual product labels, compound ingredients and cross-contact; no allergen-free certification.
fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

description: Thin rice pancakes filled with chickpeas and cabbage, with a tangy peanut dressing.
method: Whisk the rice flour with 90 g of the water and one third of the oil. Rest for 10 minutes. Finely chop the cabbage, onion and ginger.
Cook the vegetables in another third of the oil with 17.5 g of the water for 7–8 minutes. Stir in the cumin and cooked, drained chickpeas and heat through.
Brush a non-stick pan with the remaining oil. Use all the batter to make three thin pancakes, cooking each for 2–3 minutes per side until the rice flour is fully cooked.
Blend the peanuts, lime juice and remaining 17.5 g water. Fill all the pancakes with all the chickpeas and vegetables, scatter with coriander and serve with all the dressing.
notes: An unfermented rice-pancake adaptation; batter strength needs a kitchen trial.

description: Small coconut flatbreads with warm cabbage, carrot and mustard seeds.
method: Mix the flour, desiccated coconut and 35 g of the water into a soft dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest for 10 minutes.

Heat the oil in a covered pan, add the mustard seeds and cover until they begin to pop. Add finely shredded cabbage, onion and carrot, the turmeric and remaining 5 g water. Cover and cook over low heat for 8–10 minutes until tender. Stir in the lime juice.

Divide the dough into two. Flatten between non-stick sheets and dry-cook in a hot non-stick pan for 3–4 minutes per side until cooked throughout. Serve both roti with all the vegetables and their juices.

description: A soft rice and lentil bowl with vegetables, coconut, ginger and gentle spices.

description: Soft steamed buns with a savoury cabbage, mushroom and white-bean filling.
method: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and 40 g lukewarm water into a soft dough. Knead for 6–8 minutes, cover and leave in a warm place for about 45 minutes until puffy.

Finely chop the cabbage, mushroom, onion and ginger. Cook in two thirds of the olive oil with the remaining 5 g water for 8–10 minutes until tender and no loose liquid remains. Mash in the cooked, drained navy beans, soy sauce and sesame oil. Cool.

Divide the dough into three. Flatten between non-stick sheets without extra flour. Fill with all the bean mixture and pinch closed. Brush the bases with the remaining olive oil and set on parchment squares. Rest for 10 minutes.
Steam over a separate pan of boiling water for 15 minutes, keeping the buns clear of the water. Turn off the heat, leave covered for 3 minutes and serve all three buns.
notes: Estimated time includes proofing; proofing varies with room temperature.

description: Lettuce cups with tender chicken, crunchy vegetables, a peanut dressing and crisp rice pancakes.
method: Whisk the rice flour with 75 g of the water and half the rapeseed oil. Rest for 10 minutes. Steam the chicken until its centre reaches 75°C for 30 seconds, then shred it, retaining the edible juices.

Brush a non-stick pan with the remaining rapeseed oil. Use all the batter to make two very thin rice pancakes, cooking for 2–3 minutes per side until fully cooked and crisp at the edges. Cut into wedges.
Blend the peanuts, sesame oil, lime juice, soy sauce, ginger and remaining 25 g water into a dressing.
Divide all the chicken, finely sliced cucumber and carrot between the lettuce leaves. Spoon over all the dressing and serve with all the pancake wedges.

All weighed oil, sauces, dressings and edible cooking juices are included. No guessed nutrient reduction for soaking, boiling, leaching, oil left in a pan or discarded cooking water.
Food composition values are typical averages; the exact purchased product, cultivar and finished cooked dish may differ. Product substitutions require recalculation.
Energy sums reported database energy. CoFID and USDA energy conventions differ; a 4/9/4 macro reconstruction is not silently substituted.
Allergens and countable fluid require product/kitchen verification. Arithmetic completeness is not clinical or regulatory certification.

vegan.basis: Ingredient specification excludes flesh, eggs and dairy; egg-free pasta required where used.

vegetarian.basis: No meat or fish; vegetarian-rennet cheese required where used.

mediterranean.label: Mediterranean-style

dash.label: DASH-style

description: Garlicky black beans and rice with a bright cabbage, parsley and lime salad.
method: Cook the rice with 65 g of the measured water, covered, for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.

Soften the chopped onion and garlic in two thirds of the oil for 5 minutes. Add the cooked, drained black beans, remaining 15 g water and pepper. Simmer for 5–7 minutes, mashing a spoonful of beans to thicken.
Toss the shredded cabbage and chopped parsley with the remaining oil and lime juice. Serve all the beans, rice and salad.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.
allergenNote: Recipe-ingredient flags only. Check actual product labels, compound ingredients and cross-contact; no allergen-free certification.
fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

description: Plantain and black-eyed pea fritters with ginger, groundnuts and lime-dressed cabbage.
method: Use black-eyed peas previously boiled without salt and drained. Mash with the weighed peeled ripe plantain, rice flour, finely chopped onion, ginger, cumin and all the measured water.
Form four thin patties. Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and cook over medium-low heat for 5–6 minutes per side until the plantain and flour are fully cooked and the centres are steaming hot.
Toss the shredded cabbage with the lime juice and chopped peanuts. Serve all four fritters with all the cabbage.

description: Black-eyed peas in a ginger and tomato sauce, served over soft polenta.
method: Bring 130 g of the water to a gentle simmer. Whisk in the cornmeal and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring often, until fully tender. Cover off the heat if ready early.
Meanwhile soften the chopped onion, ginger and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add chopped tomato, paprika, chilli and remaining 50 g water and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the cooked, drained black-eyed peas and simmer for 5–7 minutes until hot and thickened. Serve all the stew over all the polenta.
notes: Ghanaian-inspired bean stew with a polenta accompaniment. Cooking time assumes fine standard cornmeal, not an instant packet.

description: Red lentils and vegetables in a groundnut sauce with a warm homemade flatbread.
method: Mix the flour with 25 g of the water to make a dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest for 10 minutes. Finely chop the vegetables, garlic and ginger and grind the peanuts.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika and tomato puree and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the rinsed red lentils, carrot, cabbage, ground peanuts and remaining 200 g water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are soft, stirring regularly.
Roll the dough between non-stick sheets without extra flour. Dry-cook in a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side until cooked throughout. Serve all the stew with the whole flatbread.
notes: West African groundnut-stew inspiration; not a specific traditional national recipe.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

description: Lasagne layered with white beans, roasted peppers, ricotta and a walnut topping.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C, or 180°C fan. Finely dice the pepper and onion. Cook in half the oil for 8 minutes. Add crushed garlic, cooked drained navy beans and 20 g of the measured water and simmer for 3 minutes. Mash some beans to thicken.
In a small pan, stir the flour into one quarter of the oil. Gradually whisk in the milk and remaining 45 g water. Simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in the ricotta, chopped basil and pepper.

Use no-preboil dry white lasagne sheets. Layer all the beans, pasta and sauce in a small baking dish, with sauce covering every pasta edge. Chop the walnuts and mix with the remaining oil for the topping.

Cover tightly and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover, scatter over all the walnut topping and bake for another 8–10 minutes until the pasta is tender and the centre is steaming hot. Rest for 5 minutes and serve the whole bake.
Use vegetarian-rennet cheese for the vegetarian version specified here.

description: A turkey and leek filling under a crisp, crumbly walnut pastry lid.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C, or 180°C fan. Grind the walnuts finely. Mix with 45 g of the flour, 17 g of the oil and 20 g of the water to make a dough. Cover and rest while making the filling.

Dice the turkey and slice the leek and carrot thinly. Cook in the remaining 11 g oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining 5 g flour and thyme, then gradually add the milk and remaining 90 g water. Simmer for 8–10 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the parsley and pepper and transfer all the filling and sauce to a small pie dish. Roll the pastry between non-stick sheets without extra flour and place over the top. Make a steam slit.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the pastry is cooked and the centre of the turkey filling reaches 75°C for 30 seconds. Serve the whole pie.
notes: Walnut-and-oil pastry replaces commercial puff pastry. Pastry handling needs a kitchen trial.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

description: Cod and parsley cakes with warm rice, a creamy cabbage salad and chopped walnuts.
method: Cook the rice with 70 g of the measured water, covered, for 12–15 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes.
Finely chop or pulse the cod. Mix with the egg white, rice flour, half the parsley, half the lemon juice and pepper. Form four thin cakes.
Heat three quarters of the oil in a non-stick pan. Cook the cakes for 4–5 minutes per side until fully set, opaque and steaming hot in the centres.

Mix the mayonnaise, remaining oil, remaining lemon juice and remaining 30 g water. Toss with the shredded cabbage, sliced cucumber, remaining parsley and walnuts. Serve all the cakes with all the rice and salad.

description: A fragrant chickpea and vegetable tagine with lemony almond couscous.
method: Soften the chopped onion in three fifths of the oil for 5 minutes. Add cumin, cinnamon and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add diced carrot, courgette and tomato, cooked drained chickpeas and 65 g of the measured water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender.
Bring the remaining 100 g water to a boil in a separate pan. Stir in the couscous, cover, turn off the heat and leave for 5–7 minutes.
Fluff the couscous and fold in the remaining oil, chopped almonds and half the lemon juice. Add the remaining lemon juice and chopped coriander to the tagine. Serve both whole portions.

description: Homemade ravioli filled with ricotta and walnuts, with basil oil and green beans.
method: Mix the flour and 30 g beaten egg into a firm dough. Knead for 5–7 minutes, cover and rest for 15 minutes. The measured water is for the sauce, not the dough.

Mix the ricotta with finely chopped walnuts, half the basil, half the lemon juice and black pepper. Roll the dough very thinly between non-stick sheets without extra flour. Make six large ravioli, dividing all the filling between them and pinching the edges firmly.
Steam the green beans for 6–8 minutes until tender. Poach the ravioli in a separate pan of unsalted water for 4–5 minutes until the pasta and egg are cooked throughout. Lift out carefully.
Warm the oil, measured water, remaining lemon juice and remaining basil gently in a pan. Turn all the ravioli and beans in the sauce and serve, including any loose filling.
Use vegetarian-rennet cheese for the vegetarian version specified here.
notes: Fresh ravioli dough and seal strength need practical testing. No nutrient deduction for poaching losses is assumed.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.
allergenNote: Recipe-ingredient flags only. Check actual product labels, compound ingredients and cross-contact; no allergen-free certification.
fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

description: Baked cod with coriander rice, crunchy lime slaw and avocado.
method: Blend the pepper, coriander, garlic and all the measured water. Put in a small pan with the dry rice and half the oil. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 15–18 minutes until tender. Rest covered for 5 minutes.
Brush the cod with one quarter of the oil and half the lime juice. Bake at 200°C, or 180°C fan, for 12–15 minutes until opaque, steaming hot and flaking easily.

Mix the mayonnaise, remaining oil and remaining lime juice. Toss with the shredded cabbage and carrot. Serve all the fish and edible baking juices with all the green rice, slaw and weighed avocado flesh.

description: A coconut rice and hake bake with a golden egg-white topping and crisp lime slaw.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C, or 180°C fan. Put the rice, desiccated coconut, crushed garlic, half the oil and all the measured water in a small pan. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes.
Transfer the partially cooked rice and all its liquid to a small baking dish. Nestle in the hake pieces. Pour the weighed egg white over the surface and cover tightly.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until the rice is tender, the egg white is fully set and the fish is opaque, steaming hot and flaking easily. Uncover for the last 3 minutes if needed.
Mix the mayonnaise, remaining oil, lime juice and chopped coriander. Toss with shredded cabbage and carrot. Serve the whole bake with all the slaw and all edible baking juices.
notes: Brazilian-inspired coconut and fish flavours. Countable fluid and bake hydration need measuring in a kitchen trial.

Mix the remaining oil, lemon juice and pepper. Toss with finely shredded cabbage and chopped walnuts. Serve all the skewers, edible pan juices, couscous and salad.

description: Tender cabbage leaves filled with barley, mushrooms, walnuts and homemade seitan.
method: Mix 20 g pure vital wheat gluten with 30 g of the water into a dough. Knead for 2 minutes, rest for 5 minutes, flatten to 1 cm thick and steam over a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes until firm and fully cooked. Keep the entire portion and chop finely.
Simmer the barley in 120 g of the water, covered, for 15 minutes. Add the rice and cook for another 15–20 minutes until both grains are tender, keeping all liquid.

Steam the cabbage leaves until flexible, finely chopping any edible stalk trimmings. Cook chopped onion, garlic, mushrooms and cabbage trimmings in three quarters of the oil for 6–8 minutes. Mix with all the cooked grains, seitan, walnuts, thyme and pepper.

Divide the entire filling between three large cabbage leaves, fold in the sides and roll. Put chopped tomato, paprika, remaining oil and remaining 80 g water in a covered casserole. Add the rolls and simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender and steaming hot. Serve all the rolls and sauce.
notes: This expanded-batch version uses homemade seitan in place of the earlier white beans. Source calculations reflect the exact revised ingredients. Wheat/gluten allergen applies.

description: A mild coconut and tofu curry with cabbage, peppers and basmati rice.
method: Cook the rice with 100 g of the measured water, covered, for 12–15 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes. Use regular calcium-sulphate tofu, gently drained without pressing, and cut the weighed tofu into cubes.
Soften chopped onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin, coriander and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add shredded cabbage, diced pepper and tomato, desiccated coconut, tofu and remaining 55 g water. Cover and simmer gently for 10–12 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the tofu is hot.
Stir in the lime juice and serve all the curry with all the rice.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.
allergenNote: Recipe-ingredient flags only. Check actual product labels, compound ingredients and cross-contact; no allergen-free certification.
fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

sourceAssumptions: Edible input weights exclude shells, stones, bones and inedible peel. Cooked legumes and cooked potatoes are weighed after cooking and draining.
All weighed oil, sauces, dressings and edible cooking juices are included. No guessed nutrient reduction for soaking, boiling, leaching, oil left in a pan or discarded cooking water.
Food composition values are typical averages; the exact purchased product, cultivar and finished cooked dish may differ. Product substitutions require recalculation.
Energy sums reported database energy. CoFID and USDA energy conventions differ; a 4/9/4 macro reconstruction is not silently substituted.
Allergens and countable fluid require product/kitchen verification. Arithmetic completeness is not clinical or regulatory certification.

description: Spiced turkey kebabs with a warm flatbread and cool cucumber yoghurt.
method: Mix the flour, measured water and 6 g of the oil into a dough. Knead briefly, cover and rest for 10 minutes.

Mince plain turkey breast at home. Mix with the egg white, cornmeal, very finely chopped onion and tomato, half the coriander leaves, ground cumin and coriander, and chilli. Form four thin, compact patties.
Heat 16 g of the oil in a non-stick pan. Cook the kebabs over medium heat for 5–6 minutes per side until the centres reach 75°C for 30 seconds. Keep edible pan juices.

Roll the dough between non-stick sheets and dry-cook for 2–3 minutes per side until cooked through. Mix the Greek-style yoghurt, diced cucumber, lemon juice, remaining 6 g oil and remaining coriander. Serve all the kebabs, flatbread, juices and yoghurt.

description: Tofu cakes with basil and ginger, served with rice and warm sesame cabbage.
method: Cook the short-grain rice with 55 g of the measured water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes.

Mash the weighed regular calcium-sulphate tofu, gently drained without pressing. Mix with the rice flour, finely chopped basil, garlic, ginger and 20 g of the measured water. Rest for 5 minutes, then form four small, thin cakes.
Heat 17 g of the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan. Cook the cakes for 5–6 minutes per side until firm and the centres are fully cooked.

Cook the shredded cabbage and sliced pepper in the remaining 5 g rapeseed oil and remaining 25 g water for 5–6 minutes. Stir in the sesame oil, soy sauce, lime juice and chopped peanuts. Serve all the cakes, rice and vegetables.
notes: Regular-tofu cake texture needs a kitchen trial.

Fill both pepper halves, spooning any extra filling around them. Top with all the grated Cheddar and bake for 15–20 minutes until the peppers are tender and the filling is steaming hot. Serve the entire dish with all the weighed avocado flesh, lime juice and coriander.

description: Quick-seared beef, onions and peppers with rice, tomato and fresh avocado.
method: Cook the rice with all the measured water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes. Slice the beef across the grain and cut the onion, pepper and tomato into wedges.
Heat three quarters of the oil in a wok. Sear the beef for 2–3 minutes, then add the onion, pepper and garlic. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes.
Add the tomato, soy sauce, vinegar and pepper. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, ensuring the beef surfaces are thoroughly seared and everything is hot.
Mix the weighed avocado flesh with the remaining oil and chopped coriander. Serve all the stir-fry and sauce with all the rice and avocado.

description: A gently spiced lentil and walnut bake with apple, raisins and a golden egg topping.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C, or 170°C fan. Soak the bread in 20 g of the milk, keeping all the milk.

Cook chopped onion and grated cored apple in the oil for 6 minutes. Add cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, vinegar, raisins, cooked drained green lentils and chopped walnuts. Stir in all the soaked bread and milk and the pepper.

Spoon into a small baking dish. Beat the whole egg, weighed egg white and remaining 25 g milk and pour over the top. Bake for 25–30 minutes until the topping is completely set and filling is steaming hot.
Meanwhile cook the rice in all the measured water, covered, for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes. Serve the whole bake with all the rice.

description: Savoury oat pancakes with carrots and white beans, with lemon yoghurt.
method: Grind the oats to a coarse flour. Mix with the egg white and measured water and rest for 10 minutes.
Mash the cooked, drained navy beans and stir into the batter with finely grated carrot, chives and pepper.

Heat all the oil in a non-stick pan and cook three thin pancakes for 4–5 minutes per side until fully set and the carrots are tender. Mix the yoghurt and lemon juice and serve with all three pancakes.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.
allergenNote: Recipe-ingredient flags only. Check actual product labels, compound ingredients and cross-contact; no allergen-free certification.
fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

Food composition values are typical averages; the exact purchased product, cultivar and finished cooked dish may differ. Product substitutions require recalculation.

description: A gently spiced brown rice and lentil pilaf with carrots and cabbage.
method: Cook the brown rice with 130 g of the water, covered, for 15 minutes. Rinse the white rice and red lentils.
Heat the oil in a second pan. Cook finely shredded carrot, cabbage and ginger for 4 minutes. Stir in cumin and paprika for 30 seconds.

Add all the partially cooked brown rice and its liquid, white rice, lentils and remaining 120 g water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until all grains and lentils are tender. Stir in the coriander and serve the entire portion.

description: Homemade lemon seitan with pearl barley, white beans and sweet vegetables.
method: Mix the vital wheat gluten with 35 g of the water. Knead for 2 minutes, rest for 5 minutes, flatten to 1 cm thick and steam over a separate pan of water for 20–25 minutes until firm and cooked throughout. Retain the whole seitan portion.
Meanwhile simmer the dry barley with the remaining 180 g water, covered, for 30–35 minutes until tender, retaining any liquid.
Finely dice the carrot and pepper and cook in all the oil in a covered pan for 8–10 minutes until tender. Add the cooked, drained navy beans and diced cooked seitan and heat through.
Fold all the barley and its liquid into the vegetables with the lemon juice, parsley and pepper. Serve the entire portion.
notes: Use pure vital wheat gluten, not ordinary flour; wheat/gluten allergen applies.

description: Brown rice baked with spinach, carrots and egg, with chive yoghurt.
method: Simmer the brown rice in 105 g of the water for 15 minutes. Add the white rice and remaining 45 g water and cook covered for another 12–15 minutes until tender.
Heat the oven to 190°C, or 170°C fan. Finely grate the carrot and chop the spinach. Cook in the oil for 5 minutes, then mix with all the rice and any liquid.
Beat the weighed whole egg and egg white with the pepper and mix through the warm rice. Put in a small dish and bake for 18–22 minutes until fully set and steaming hot.
Mix the yoghurt and chives and serve with the entire bake.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

description: Lime baked fish with rice, avocado and a creamy cabbage and carrot slaw.
method: Cook the rice with all the measured water, covered, for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.
Brush the cod with 10 g of the oil and half the lime juice. Bake at 200°C, or 180°C fan, for 12–15 minutes until opaque and steaming hot.

Mix mayonnaise, remaining 15 g oil, remaining lime juice, chopped coriander and pepper. Toss with shredded cabbage and carrot. Serve all the fish and edible juices with all the rice, weighed avocado flesh and slaw.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

description: A substantial lentil and walnut bobotie with apple, raisins, a golden egg topping and rice.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C, or 170°C fan. Soak the bread in 25 g of the milk, retaining all the milk. Cook the rice with all the measured water, covered, for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.

Soften chopped onion and grated cored apple in the oil for 6 minutes. Add all the spices, vinegar, raisins, chopped walnuts, cooked drained lentils, soaked bread and milk, and pepper. Cook for 3 minutes.

Transfer the entire filling to a small dish. Beat the weighed whole egg and egg white with the remaining 25 g milk and pour over. Bake for 25–30 minutes until completely set and steaming hot. Serve the whole bake with all the rice.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.
allergenNote: Recipe-ingredient flags only. Check actual product labels, compound ingredients and cross-contact; no allergen-free certification.
fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

description: A warming beef and black-eyed pea stew with soft polenta.
method: Bring 210 g of the measured water to a simmer, whisk in the cornmeal and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes until tender, stirring frequently.
Dice the beef small and finely chop the vegetables and garlic. Brown the beef surfaces in all the oil for 3 minutes. Add onion, carrot, garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 5 minutes.

Add chopped tomato, cooked drained black-eyed peas and remaining 30 g water. Cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until the carrot is tender and stew is steaming hot. Stir in parsley and pepper and serve all the stew over all the polenta.
calculationBasis: One complete recipe = one serving. Sum quantityG/100 × source nutrient/100 g, without rounding intermediate values. Salt = total sodium × 2.5/1000.

fluidAssessment: Finished countable fluid not measured. Do not infer zero, and do not treat ingredient water or intrinsic food moisture as measured clinical countable fluid.

description: Salmon and leeks baked under a light egg and rice topping.
method: Cook the rice with 115 g of the measured water in a covered pan for 12–15 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes. Heat the oven to 190°C, or 170°C fan.

Slice the leek and soften in all the oil for 6 minutes. Stir in the flour, then gradually add the milk and remaining 10 g water. Simmer for 3 minutes and add the salmon in small pieces, parsley, lemon juice and pepper.
Transfer all the filling to a small dish. Beat the weighed whole egg and egg white and mix with all the warm rice. Spoon over the fish.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the topping is fully set and the salmon is opaque and steaming hot. Serve the entire pie and sauce.
